resources.string: Reads the text of WhatsApp messages so it can translate them on device and draw the translation in their place. Text from other apps is never read, and nothing is sent anywhere.
Translates WhatsApp messages in place, on device.

Detects whatever language a message is in and replaces it with your language, right inside the bubble. No screen recording and no OCR — the text is read straight from WhatsApp\'s view hierarchy, and Google\'s translation models run locally, so nothing about your chats leaves the phone.
Settings → Accessibility → Installed apps → Lingo → turn on. This is the only permission normally needed.
Usually not required. Grant it only if the floating button never appears over WhatsApp.
A round globe button appears at the edge of the screen. Drag it anywhere. Tap once to translate the conversation, tap again to stop.
Defaults to your phone\'s language. Messages already in this language are left exactly as WhatsApp drew them.
Translation runs offline, so each language needs a one-off download of about 30 MB. It happens automatically the first time that language turns up — pull one down here in advance to avoid the wait.
No language packs on device yet.
Off by default, so a language you run into on mobile data still works. Turn it on to keep the 30 MB downloads off your data plan.
Could not download the %1$s pack. Check your connection.
Patches must be opaque to hide the original message, so these have to match WhatsApp\'s own bubbles.
Outlines every text node instead of translating it — red for incoming, blue for outgoing — and records what the service can see. Use this if nothing gets translated.
Ignores the conversation-list detection and translates every string on screen.
No dump yet — turn on diagnostic mode, open a WhatsApp chat, then come back.
